discovery.notes: The serial number is the part of the advertised local name after the slash ("Encharg/<serial>"); the Installer Toolkit matches devices by testing whether the advertised name CONTAINS the expected serial, so the serial substring is the stable identity. Whether the XBee 3 BLE service UUID 53da53b9 is present in the advertisement itself (vs. only after connection) is unverified — name matching is the app-confirmed path.

mac_prefixes.notes: Silicon Labs OUI of the Digi XBee 3 (EFR32) radio inside the units; observed live 2026-08-18 on one Enpower and two Encharge units. Shared with every other Silicon Labs-based product, so a ranking signal only — never sufficient alone.

device.name: Enphase IQ Battery / IQ System Controller (BLE)
device.notes:
Enphase Ensemble storage gear — Encharge/IQ Battery and the Enpower/IQ System Controller — carries a Digi XBee 3 radio (Silicon Labs EFR32 inside, hence the Silabs OUI on the BLE MAC) that serves double duty: the 2.4 GHz 802.15.4 site mesh, and a BLE interface used by installers. The BLE interface is the stock Digi XBee 3 BLE GATT service: an SRP-6a-authenticated unlock, then an encrypted pipe carrying XBee API frames; Enphase payloads ride inside XBee "User Data Relay" frames addressed to the radio's serial interface. Two payload layers exist: a simple one-byte-typed provisioning frame set (link key and Envoy serial provisioning, PAN-ID verification, pairing status, relay states, telemetry read), and a rich protobuf "object model" (EnsObjMdlMessage) used for live statistics, inventory, relay control, battery SoC/phase config and blackstart recovery. This spec covers the battery/switch units themselves; the site gateway's own REST and BLE surfaces are documented separately in enphase-envoy. Relationship to the cloud: the commissioning sequence the vendor app runs is installer-account driven, but the BLE link itself needs no cloud — use the flow-specific password in protocol_details.unlock_passwords; the link key is generated locally.
INTEGRATION SCOPE: `supported` means the mobile client can discover these units and run the SRP-6a/AES unlock followed by read-only status queries types 4, 5 and 8. It does not expose provisioning, relay, grid or other installer control writes, and no live hardware unlock has been performed. This is the Digi XBee 3 BLE protocol, not an XBee Series 2 / "XBee2" profile. Communications Kit 2 is a separate product boundary whose GATT services and credentials are not established and are not covered here.

openness.notes: No public protocol documentation from Enphase; commissioning is gated behind an installer certification program, and battery control flows through the gateway and Enlighten cloud. The BLE link layer itself is Digi's documented XBee 3 BLE protocol; the Enphase payload layer documented here is app-derived.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: The BLE interface is live whenever the unit is powered; there is no pairing mode and no button. Access control is entirely the SRP-6a unlock.

exclusivity.notes: One BLE connection at a time is reported for the XBee 3 BLE stack on Digi's community forum, not in Digi's reference documentation. SRP stores a verifier for one shared password, not per-client records, so any number of clients that know the password can unlock in turn and none evicts another.
exclusivity.recovery: Make sure no installer tablet or phone running the Installer Toolkit is connected to the unit; disconnect it, then connect.

pairing.notes: The real gate is the Digi XBee 3 BLE unlock: SRP-6a (RFC 5054 1024-bit group, SHA-256) with the fixed username "apiservice" and the shared password above, after which every frame is AES-encrypted with the negotiated session key. The link layer asks for nothing and nothing bonds; a client holds no stored credential beyond the password, and no Enphase account or cloud is involved at this layer — the installer-account dependency sits in the commissioning workflow, not the radio. See the setup method for the handshake and the services block for the frame layer.

pin.notes: Reviewed Ensemble provisioning, link-key verification and live-data paths expect the shared static value 030609. Separate range-test and gateway helpers default to "password"; that helper value is not the established Ensemble battery credential. A stock XBee 3 ships with SRP salt 0 (authentication disabled), so the production provisioning is Enphase-specific. Acceptance on every model/firmware is unverified; these are product-wide constants, not per-unit secrets.

unpair.clears: Every client's access at once: there is one shared password, so re-keying it is the only revocation, and it is total.
unpair.notes: Revocation means changing the password: an authenticated client writes a new SRP salt and verifier (the XBee $S and $V/$W/$X/$Y settings, which Digi's libraries derive from a password) and saves them. Two cautions before anyone does it. Enphase's installer app only knows the default, so a re-keyed unit is one the installer can no longer commission or service over BLE. And setting the salt to zero does not open the unit — on XBee 3 it disables BLE authentication, locking every client out. Neither has been tried on an Enphase unit; whether Enphase's firmware lets these settings be changed over the BLE channel is inferred from the stock XBee 3 behaviour.

issued_to_client: None — the client authenticates with the flow-specific XBee BLE password (030609 on the reviewed Ensemble paths; see protocol_details.unlock_passwords)
credentials.notes: The 16-byte 802.15.4 link key is generated by the app with SecureRandom at commissioning time and pushed to every Ensemble device. All-zero and all-0xFF candidates are rejected, as is a candidate with 13 zero bytes followed by the reserved 03 06 09 prefix. That prefix is NOT a demonstrated fallback mesh key. Possession of the BLE unlock password may yield the site mesh key — meaningful for site security, and the reason this layer deserves the encrypted channel.
stored_on_device: 802.15.4 site PAN ID and link key

factory_reset.effect: Not documented in this project. Frame type 2 (RESET_DEV) exists in the provisioning frame set and is app-reachable, but its exact effect (radio-only vs. full de-commission) is unknown; do not poke it on a live site.

steps.action: Consult the model's install manual; de-commissioning is normally done by an installer via the gateway.

ble.protocol: Digi XBee 3 BLE + Enphase relay payload (see services)

methods.description: Connect to the unit's XBee 3 BLE service and run the SRP-6a unlock (XBee API frame 0x2C, username "apiservice") with the reviewed Ensemble password "030609". The four-frame exchange yields a 32-byte session key and separate 12-byte nonces for AES-256-CTR in each direction; verify the 32-byte proof before encrypted relay traffic. All values are app-derived and no live unlock was performed.

steps.action: Connect and discover the XBee 3 BLE service; subscribe to the RX characteristic f9279ee9-2cd0-410c-81cc-adf11e4e5aea.

Perform the four-frame SRP-6a unlock for user 'apiservice' using 030609 on the reviewed Ensemble paths. Verify the server's 32-byte proof. In phase 4 take bytes 32-43 as the 12-byte TX nonce for client→XBee and bytes 44-55 as the 12-byte RX nonce for XBee→client, then use the 32-byte session key with those direction-specific nonces as AES-256-CTR counter prefixes and initial remaining counter value 1.
steps.expect: Unlock response frame 0xAC reports success; subsequent traffic is AES-256-CTR encrypted with the appropriate nonce in each direction.

steps.action: Exchange Enphase frames as XBee User Data Relay (0x2D) payloads addressed to the serial interface; responses arrive as User Data Relay Output (0xAD).

setup.notes: These units are installer-commissioned, not owner-paired. The reviewed Ensemble paths push a locally generated 16-byte link key and the Envoy serial used to derive/verify the site's 802.15.4 PAN ID; a separate numeric PAN-ID write is not established. Provisioning, link-key verification and live-data access expect the shared static password "030609". The value "password" belongs to separate range-test/gateway helpers, not these Ensemble paths. Both are app-derived constants, not per-unit secrets. Whether units keep advertising BLE indefinitely after commissioning is unverified — the units at the research site still beacon many months after install.

rejoin.notes: Site-mesh re-join re-runs the link-key and Envoy-serial provisioning flow and verifies the derived PAN ID; no separate numeric PAN-ID write is established. No reset is needed, and the app retries the link-key push with freshly generated keys on mismatch.

testing.notes: Advertisement identity is live-verified: a BT scan on 2026-08-18 at the owner's site found an Enpower smart switch and two Encharge (IQ Battery) units beaconing as "Enpower/<serial>" and "Encharg/<serial>" from Silicon Labs OUI MACs (04:0D:84:*). No GATT connection was attempted (production storage on a live site). Everything below the advertisement layer — GATT UUIDs, unlock handshake, relay frames, protobuf schema — is derived from clean-room static analysis of the Enphase Installer Toolkit Android app (2026-08-19), cross-checked against Digi's public XBee 3 BLE documentation and the public digi-xbee-java library. Treat the GATT/protocol layer as medium confidence until exercised on hardware.

app_static_analysis.confidence_notes: Derived from app code, not yet exercised against the units; the Digi XBee 3 BLE layer is additionally public vendor documentation.
confirms: Units are reached via the stock Digi XBee 3 BLE GATT service 53da53b9-0447-425a-b9ea-9837505eb59a (TX 7dddca00-3e05-4651-9254-44074792c590, RX f9279ee9-2cd0-410c-81cc-adf11e4e5aea), bundled com.digi.xbee library.

Unlock is a four-frame SRP-6a exchange on XBee BLE frame 0x2C/response 0xAC (username 'apiservice'). Reviewed Ensemble provisioning, link-key verification and live-data paths expect '030609'; separate range-test/gateway helpers use 'password'. AES-256-CTR uses a verified 32-byte session key and direction-specific 12-byte nonces (follow-up static review 2026-11-08; no live unlock).
Enphase payloads ride XBee User Data Relay (0x2D) to the radio's serial interface (micropython interface for the IQ Extender); responses come back as User Data Relay Output (0xAD).

Provisioning frame types 0-9 (link key, reset, relay states, ZB pairing/commissioning status, link key read, Envoy SN write/read, Enpower telemetry read); polls use [type, 0], while write byte 1 can be a length, as in [0x01][0x10][16 key bytes]. The reserved 03 06 09 prefix is rejected during random-key validation, not used as a fallback key; no separate numeric PAN-ID write is established.

A protobuf object-model layer (EnsObjMdlMessage, proto2: required protover=1, required uint64 timestamp=2, oneof payload tags 3-63) carries inventory, poll/live stats, subscribe/publish, relay and secondary control, SoC/phase config, sleep mode, manual override, events and memfault diagnostics.
Discovery matches advertised name containing the device serial; no scan filter on service UUID.
app_static_analysis.source: Static analysis of the Enphase Installer Toolkit Android app (clean-room audit; derived facts only)

live_ble_scan.protocol: Passive BT scan at the owner's site: one "Enpower/<serial>" and two "Encharg/<serial>" beacons, all from Silicon Labs OUI MACs (04:0D:84:*). Identity-layer facts (names, OUI) verified; nothing connected or probed further.

channel_security.initial_counter: Initial remaining counter value 1 after the 12-byte nonce prefix.
channel_security.nonces: The server supplies two distinct 12-byte nonces, one for each direction. Use each as its direction's counter prefix; do not reuse one nonce for both directions. In phase 4 after the 32-byte proof, bytes 32-43 are the TX nonce for client→XBee and bytes 44-55 are the RX nonce for XBee→client.
channel_security.proof_and_key: Verify the server's 32-byte proof before using the 32-byte (AES-256) session key.
channel_security.relay_directions: 0x2D User Data Relay remains client-to-device; 0xAD User Data Relay Output remains device-to-client.
channel_security.srp: SRP-6a, RFC 5054 1024-bit group, SHA-256, fixed username apiservice; four-frame exchange carried by BLE Unlock 0x2C and Unlock Response 0xAC.

live_statistics.description: Poll/inventory responses decode (partly in the app's native libble-data.so) into per-device live statistics. The Encharge unit record carries: aggregated power, state of charge, number of active and ready microinverters (PCUs), inventory-updated flag, device UID, LED status, BMU state, available charge and discharge power, and phase-line assignment; nested records carry per-BMU and per-PCU statistics. Exact native byte layout not yet reversed — the protobuf path above is the documented one.

object_model.description: Rich request/response and pub/sub protocol (Square Wire classes, proto2 syntax) used for live statistics, inventory, control and blackstart recovery. Envelope message EnsObjMdlMessage: field 1 = ProtocolVer protover (required; VERSION_1_0 in use), field 2 = uint64 timestamp (required), fields 3-63 = oneof payload, one message per exchange. The poll request (tag 13) is {required string serial_num = 1, required int32 dm_group_id = 2}; its response (tag 14) carries the live statistics the app's device-details screens render. The device can also publish asynchronously (publish req/rsp tags 9/10 after subscribe 7/8).

payload_tags.32/33: Encharge SoC config req/rsp (also used to push battery phase assignment)

provisioning_frames.description: Simple frame set used at commissioning, built by the app's XBee BLE manager. Request byte 0 is the frame type. Poll requests are [type, 0], but byte 1 is NOT universally zero: writes can use it as a length, as in [01][10][16 key bytes] (18 bytes) and the length-prefixed Envoy serial write. Responses echo the type in byte 0, and the payload is everything after the first two bytes. A separate numeric PAN-ID write is not established; Envoy serial is used to derive/verify the PAN ID.

frame_types.1: LINK_KEY — push the 16-byte 802.15.4 site link key; full frame is [0x01][0x10][16 key bytes] (18 bytes)
frame_types.2: RESET_DEV — device reset (effect unverified; treat as destructive)
frame_types.6: ZB_READ_LINK_KEY — read back the stored link key
frame_types.7: Gateway serial write — write the gateway (Envoy) serial number; layout in write_envoy_sn
frame_types.8: ZB_READ_ENVOY_SN — read back the gateway serial (used by the app to derive/verify the site PAN ID; mismatch is a first-class PAN_ID_MISMATCH error)

write_envoy_sn.notes: The gateway serial is written as ASCII bytes after type 0x07 and its one-byte length.

related_specs: enphase-envoy — the site gateway: LAN REST API, mDNS identity, and the gateway-side BLE services (connectivity ed453f0f-*, ensemble 5c498caa-*, validation 19f4de83-*, devices ba808b5a-*, OTA 57c44b4a-*) this site's units are commissioned to report to.
enphase_relay_protocol.transport: Byte stream inside XBee User Data Relay (0x2D, outgoing) and User Data Relay Output (0xAD, incoming) frames, destination interface SERIAL (MICROPYTHON on the IQ Extender).

unlock_passwords.notes: Reviewed Ensemble provisioning, existing-device link-key verification and live-data paths all expect the shared static value "030609". The value "password" is confined to separate range-test and gateway connection helpers and is not the established Ensemble battery credential. Acceptance on every model/firmware still requires owner-authorized validation; no live unlock was attempted and no per-unit secret is inferred.

characteristics.name: TX (client writes XBee API frames)
characteristics.notes: Write XBee API frames here. After unlock the app wraps Enphase payloads in User Data Relay (0x2D) frames.

characteristics.name: RX (device notifies XBee API frames)
characteristics.notes: Notifications carry the device's XBee API frames — BLE Unlock Response (0xAC) during the handshake, then User Data Relay Output (0xAD) frames carrying Enphase responses. The standard CCCD (0x2902) is used to enable notifications.

services.name: Digi XBee 3 BLE (XBee BLE Service)
services.notes: The stock Digi XBee 3 BLE service — the Enpower/Encharge/IQ Extender BLE interface is exactly this, confirmed in the bundled com.digi.xbee.api Android library and matching Digi's public XBee 3 BLE documentation. XBee API frames are written to TX and received on RX; before the four-frame SRP-6a unlock completes only BLE Unlock frames (0x2C) are accepted. Verify the 32-byte proof, then use the 32-byte session key for AES-256-CTR in both directions, with the appropriate direction-specific 12-byte nonce as counter prefix and initial remaining counter value 1 (the library applies the cipher in its GATT callbacks). XBee API frame types in play (public digi-xbee-java APIFrameType): 0x2C BLE Unlock, 0xAC BLE Unlock Response, 0x2D User Data Relay (client→device), 0xAD User Data Relay Output (device→client). Enphase payloads are the user-data field of the relay frames, addressed to XBeeLocalInterface.SERIAL (XBeeLocalInterface.MICROPYTHON for the IQ Extender).
